t: Cooperative Graceful Degradation in Containerized Clouds
pb: Cloud operators lack a mechanism to automatically perform graceful degradation of applications during failures or capacity crunch while simultaneously satisfying application availability requirements and operator infrastructure objectives.
me: Phoenix uses criticality tags on containers to distinguish critical from non-critical services, then applies diagonal scaling—turning off non-critical containers during capacity crunch to free resources for critical services. A Kubernetes-atop controller implements this cooperative graceful degradation by jointly optimizing for both application-defined criticality constraints and operator-level infrastructure objectives. Phoenix handles failures in a cluster of 100,000 nodes within 10 seconds.
nv: Diagonal scaling: a cooperative degradation primitive that leverages application-supplied criticality tags to selectively deactivate non-critical containers, maximizing critical service availability during large-scale failures.

mx.other: critical service availability improved up to 2x during large-scale failures; handles 100K node cluster failures within 10 seconds

th: Cooperative graceful degradation for containerized cloud resilience

t: H-Houdini: Scalable Invariant Learning
pb: Formal hardware verification via invariant learning (e.g., IC3/PDR) does not scale to large hardware designs because the invariant search space grows exponentially with state size, causing state-of-the-art tools to time out on real-world RTL designs.
me: H-Houdini extends the Houdini invariant-learning algorithm with scalability improvements targeting large hardware designs. The likely approach involves decomposing the hardware design into manageable sub-modules or abstract components, learning invariants compositionally (e.g., assume-guarantee or abstraction-refinement), and propagating learned invariants across the design hierarchy to avoid full-state enumeration. Specific algorithmic details are not disclosed in the available abstract.
nv: Scalable extension of Houdini-style invariant learning to large hardware designs that previously exceeded the capacity of existing formal verification tools.

mx.other: Scalability to larger hardware designs than prior tools; specific numbers not in abstract

th: Scalable invariant learning for large hardware formal verification

t: Hardware Sentinel: Protecting Software Applications from Hardware Silent Data Corruptions
pb: Silent Data Corruptions (SDCs) caused by silicon defects in CPUs propagate undetected through large-scale data center applications, causing unpredictable failures (segfaults, crashes, log anomalies) that are difficult to attribute to hardware without systematic cross-layer analysis.
me: Hardware Sentinel is a top-down framework that correlates software-layer failure indicators—segmentation faults, core dumps, application crashes, and structured logs—with underlying hardware-layer defect signals across CPUs. It builds statistical models linking application failure patterns to CPU hardware identities, enabling SDC attribution across diverse workload, kernel, and hardware configurations. The framework was validated over 6 years of failure data spanning 13 workloads across 27 data center regions, using fleet-wide telemetry ingestion and cross-referencing with out-of-production (Fleetscanner) and in-production (Ripple) hardware tests.
nv: A production-validated, software-failure-driven SDC detection framework that identifies defective CPUs from application-layer signals without requiring dedicated hardware test circuits, achieving broader coverage than existing hardware testing methods.

mx.other: SDC detection coverage: 1.74x over Fleetscanner, 1.92x over Ripple

th: software-driven silent data corruption detection in production fleets

t: ElasticMiter: Formally Verified Dataflow Circuit Rewrites
pb: Dataflow circuits produced by high-level synthesis (HLS) compilers cannot be optimized via standard sequential equivalence verification because their latency-insensitive handshake semantics are incompatible with traditional notions of sequential equivalence, leaving no sound basis for automated datapath simplification.
me: ElasticMiter develops a generic equivalence verification framework for latency-insensitive dataflow circuits by constructing a miter circuit that detects functional divergence under all possible token arrival patterns. It then defines a graph rewriting system over dataflow circuit DAGs where each rewrite rule is verified by the framework before being applied, guaranteeing the rewritten circuit is equivalent to the original. The approach handles elastic buffering, fork/join nodes, and control tokens that are absent in traditional sequential circuits.
nv: The first formally verified dataflow circuit transformation system that constructs a latency-insensitive miter to prove graph rewrite rules sound for HLS-generated circuits.

mx.area: circuit simplification (area reduction) shown via graph rewrites

th: formally verified dataflow circuit optimization for HLS

t: Robustness Verification for Checking Crash Consistency of Non-volatile Memory
pb: Programs using non-volatile memory (NVM) must explicitly flush pending stores to guarantee persistence; developers routinely miss or mis-order these flushes. Existing crash-consistency checkers are testing-based and require user guidance, leaving the correctness of NVM programs unverified in the general case.
me: The paper introduces a robustness property for NVM crash consistency and proves that checking whether a post-crash NVM state is reachable from a given pre-crash execution reduces to validity of that execution under additional ordering constraints. A search-based algorithm enumerates all partial pre-crash executions and candidate NVM states, then dispatches each reachability query to an SMT solver via symbolic encoding of the program. The approach is integrated into the DPLL(T) framework to prune the search space, and is implemented in the prototype tool PMVerify.
nv: Reduction of crash-consistency checking to SMT-based reachability under the NVM memory consistency model, enabling the first fully automated robustness verification without user-provided test inputs.

mx.other: Bug detection competitive with PSan on PMDK benchmarks

th: formal crash-consistency verification for NVM

t: Will We Ever have Truly Secure Operating Systems?
pb: Operating system kernels remain a dominant attack surface despite decades of security research; formal proofs of OS security have historically been limited to small microkernels and have not scaled to binary-level or general-purpose OS kernels.
me: The paper surveys the seL4 microkernel verification program, which produced a proof chain from C implementation correctness, down to binary-level verification, through to security enforcement proofs (confidentiality, integrity) and sound worst-case execution-time analysis, covering 4 ISAs. The approach uses interactive theorem provers (Isabelle/HOL) to formally connect abstract security policies to compiled binary behavior, then discusses speculative early-stage work on extending this methodology to a provably secure general-purpose OS.
nv: First complete proof chain from OS implementation to binary code to security enforcement properties across multiple ISAs, including sound worst-case execution time, for seL4.

mx.other: Proofs cover 4 ISAs; first binary-level + security enforcement proof chain for an OS kernel

th: formal OS security verification

t: Dynamic Partial Deadlock Detection and Recovery via Garbage Collection
pb: Concurrent message-passing programs in Go are susceptible to partial deadlocks where goroutines block indefinitely on channels, causing severe memory leaks in long-running systems. Existing techniques cannot both detect and automatically recover from these partial deadlocks at runtime.
me: GOLF extends Go's garbage collector marking phase to soundly approximate goroutine liveness: a goroutine is considered live only if its channel references are reachable from the GC root set. During GC marking, goroutines blocked on channels with no live senders are flagged as deadlocked. Detected deadlocked goroutines are then automatically cancelled or cleaned up to free memory and restore system progress. The detection integrates directly into the existing GC pause with minimal overhead.
nv: Using the garbage collector's reachability marking phase as a sound liveness approximation for goroutines, enabling automatic partial deadlock detection and recovery without separate runtime monitors.

mx.accuracy: 94% detection rate on microbenchmarks, 50% on industrial test suites
mx.other: 252 partial deadlocks detected in 24 hours in a live Uber service

th: GC-based partial deadlock detection and automatic recovery in Go

t: PCcheck: Persistent Concurrent Checkpointing for ML
pb: Checkpointing large ML training runs to persistent storage introduces high overhead when done at high frequency, yet infrequent checkpointing leads to long recovery times after failures — a growing problem as training scale increases and cheap spot VMs dramatically raise failure rates.
me: PCcheck introduces persistent concurrent checkpointing, where model parameter checkpoints are taken concurrently with ongoing training (overlapping checkpoint I/O with compute) while also ensuring persistence to durable storage. It uses a combination of copy-on-write snapshots of model state and pipelined multi-stage I/O to overlap CPU-to-storage transfers with GPU computation. The system tracks consistency across concurrent training steps to guarantee that the checkpoint captured is valid and recoverable, minimizing pause time during the checkpoint process.
nv: Concurrent persistent checkpointing that overlaps I/O with training compute using copy-on-write snapshots and pipelined storage transfers, achieving high-frequency durable checkpoints without proportional training overhead.

mx.other: specific numbers not available in abstract

th: concurrent persistent checkpointing for large-scale ML training fault tolerance

t: Formalising CXL Cache Coherence
pb: The CXL.cache inter-device cache coherence protocol specification (governing coherence between CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators over PCIe) contains ambiguities, redundancies, inaccuracies, and potential coherence violations that could cause incompatible vendor implementations or incorrect hardware if left unresolved.
me: The authors formalize CXL.cache as a state-transition system in the Isabelle proof assistant, modeling 20 system components (device caches, host cache, message channels, buffers, programs, transaction counter) and 68 transition rules encoding the complete legal message flows. They perform scenario verification (litmus tests from CXL message-sequence charts) to validate model faithfulness and to show that relaxing restrictions such as Snoop-pushes-GO causes coherence violations. They then prove the Single-Writer-Multiple-Reader (SWMR) property by constructing a 796-conjunct inductive invariant that implies SWMR and is preserved by all 68 rules (53,332 lemmas), using a custom super_sketch Isabelle automation tool to manage proof scale.
nv: The first mechanized, formally proven coherence property (SWMR) for the CXL.cache protocol, produced via a 796-conjunct inductive invariant and 53,332 auto-generated Isabelle lemmas, leading directly to five accepted fixes in the CXL standard.

mx.other: 53,332 Isabelle lemmas proven; 796-conjunct invariant; 211k lines of proof; 3-5 hours build time on Intel Core i9-14900HX; 12 person-months total

th: Formal mechanized verification of the CXL cache coherence protocol

t: RTL Verification for Secure Speculation Using Contract Shadow Logic
pb: Speculative execution attacks exploit microarchitectural side channels in out-of-order processors, but rigorous formal verification of hardware RTL designs against speculative security contracts has been lacking, leaving unknown vulnerabilities despite proposed mitigations.
me: Contract Shadow Logic introduces a formal RTL verification methodology that augments a processor's RTL with shadow logic encoding speculative execution contracts (defining what information a processor's speculative state may leak). The shadow logic tracks information flow through speculative pipelines at the RTL level, and model checking or equivalence checking is used to verify that no execution trace violates the contract, providing machine-checked security guarantees for the hardware design.
nv: Attaching contract-encoding shadow logic directly to processor RTL enables automated, formal verification of speculative execution security properties at the implementation level.

mx.other: formal security verification coverage (specific numbers not in abstract)

th: Formal RTL verification of speculative execution security

t: Debugger Toolchain Validation via Cross-Level Debugging
pb: Existing debugger toolchain validation techniques detect bugs in debug information by comparing execution traces between optimized and unoptimized executables, but compiler optimizations make such traces incomparable and leave bugs in debugger toolchains undetected when the unoptimized executable itself contains toolchain errors.
me: The paper introduces Cross-Level Debugging (CLD), which compares execution traces obtained from debugging the same executable using source-level and instruction-level debugging strategies within the same debugger. CLD formalizes three invariant relations—reachability preservation of program locations, order preservation for reachable locations, and value consistency at program locations—that must hold between the two trace levels regardless of optimization level. The Devil framework implements these relations as test oracles, generates diverse test programs, runs them under both debugging levels, and flags violations as toolchain bugs.
nv: Using source-level versus instruction-level debugging of the same executable as a built-in oracle, eliminating the need to compare across different executables and enabling detection of toolchain bugs even in unoptimized binaries.

mx.other: 27 new bug reports found; 18 confirmed, 12 fixed by developers in GDB and LLDB

th: Cross-level oracle-based debugger toolchain validation

t: QECC-Synth: A Layout Synthesizer for Quantum Error Correction Codes on Sparse Architectures
pb: Quantum Error Correction (QEC) codes require dense qubit connectivity that does not match the sparse qubit coupling graphs of current hardware architectures, and existing QEC circuit compilation approaches either underutilize QEC circuit structure or rely on manual, architecture-specific designs that do not generalize.
me: QECC-Synth is an automated compiler that uses the ancilla bridge technique—inserting ancilla qubits to implement long-range interactions over sparse coupling graphs—and systematically classifies the design space flexibilities of this technique. It then formulates the layout synthesis problem as a MaxSAT optimization problem over these flexibility dimensions, finding globally near-optimal ancilla placement and routing for a given QEC code and hardware architecture. This approach is architecture-agnostic and handles diverse QEC codes (e.g., surface code, color code) without manual redesign.
nv: Formulating QEC layout synthesis as a MaxSAT problem over a systematically classified ancilla bridge design space, enabling automated, architecture-agnostic compilation of diverse QEC codes onto sparse hardware.

mx.other: significantly outperforms existing methods on QEC circuit quality across diverse QEC codes and hardware architectures (exact numbers not available from abstract)

th: Automated MaxSAT-based layout synthesis for quantum error correction codes

t: Fault Escaping: Improving Robustness of DPU Enhanced Platform with Mutual Assisted VM Recovery
pb: Modern cloud servers that use DPUs to offload virtualization split VM state across the DPU SoC and the host, so a failure in either component crashes the entire machine and all hosted VMs, with no fault-tolerant mechanism designed for this split-hypervisor architecture.
me: The paper proposes fault escaping: a scheme that treats the split hypervisors on the DPU SoC and the host as redundant peers. Using hybrid synchronization, the full VM state (in a verified, consistent snapshot) is kept accessible on either the DPU or the host with minimal synchronization overhead (kilobytes of data). When one side fails, VMs migrate their state to the surviving peer and resume execution there, bypassing the failed component rather than attempting to recover it. The hybrid synchronization protocol differentiates hot and cold VM state to minimize cross-component bandwidth.
nv: Treating DPU and host hypervisors as redundant peers that can each host the full VM state, enabling VMs to escape from a failing component rather than waiting for in-place recovery.

mx.other: kilobytes of synchronization overhead (vs. full VM state transfer); VM recovery latency improvement (exact numbers not available from abstract)

th: VM fault tolerance via peer redundancy in DPU-split hypervisor architectures

t: FastFlip: Compositional SDC Resiliency Analysis
pb: Error injection analyses for Silent Data Corruption (SDC) resiliency are prohibitively expensive and must rerun from scratch after code changes, making them impractical for iterative development workflows such as regression testing.
me: FastFlip combines empirical error injection with symbolic SDC propagation analysis to enable incremental re-analysis. When code changes, it analyzes only modified sections rather than entire programs, leveraging compositional analysis to identify vulnerable instructions and guide selective compiler-level SDC detection.
nv: First approach to enable compositional and incremental error injection analysis, reanalyzing only changed program sections rather than running fresh analyses.

mx.speedup: 3.2× geomean on incremental versions; up to 17.2×

th: Incremental SDC resiliency analysis

t: Improving Native-Image Startup Performance
pb: Serverless/FaaS workloads have short lifetimes where startup time directly impacts service-level agreements. Despite AOT heap pre-initialization in GraalVM Native Image, startup remains suboptimal due to excessive page faults from poor binary layout.
me: Profile-guided binary reordering reorders code and objects in heap snapshots to minimize page faults. Proposes execution-order profiling to capture method and object access sequences. Three object ordering strategies reduce heap-related page faults. Matches profiled objects to built objects despite identity/persistence changes across Native Image builds.
nv: First profile-guided approach to reorder heap snapshot objects in AOT-compiled Native Image binaries to reduce page faults.

mx.other: 1.61× page fault reduction

th: Profile-guided startup optimization via binary reordering

t: Pattern Matching in AI Compilers and Its Formalization
pb: PyPM DSL for ML graph rewriting has complex pattern matching language borrowing from logic programming (recursive, nondeterministic, constraint-checking), making the implementation difficult to understand and verify (thousands of lines of C++).
me: Develops formal core calculus expressing PyPM pattern language semantics. Defines declarative semantics (which patterns match which terms) and algorithmic semantics (idealized interpreter). Proves equivalence between both semantics using Coq proof assistant, fully mechanized.
nv: First formal verification and specification of ML compiler pattern matching language via mechanized proofs in Coq.
th: Formal verification of ML pattern matching

t: Parallaft: Runtime-Based CPU Fault Tolerance via Heterogeneous Parallelism
pb: Increasing silicon faults in modern microprocessors create silent data corruption risks; existing software-based error detection suffers from high power and performance overhead, while state-of-the-art hardware fault-tolerance techniques are too complex for production deployment.
me: Parallaft repurposes insights from hardware heterogeneous-parallelism fault tolerance in pure software using modern OS tools: copy-on-write checkpointing, dirty-page tracking, and performance-counter synchronization. Error checking is offloaded to little cores of heterogeneous processors (e.g., Apple M2), achieving detection without dedicated hardware.
nv: Adapting hardware heterogeneous fault-tolerance concepts to software-based implementation using OS primitives and little-core offloading on commodity heterogeneous processors.
th: Software-based error detection via heterogeneous core offloading

t: PastATPG: A Hybrid ATPG Framework for Better Test Compaction with Partial Assignment SAT
pb: SAT-based ATPG generates complete assignments for all primary inputs in fanin cone, leading to pattern inflation and excessive runtime; test compaction becomes intractable as circuits grow.
me: PA-MiniSat SAT solver enabling partial assignments instead of complete assignments; full-literal watching technique and circuit-adapted branching heuristics; hybrid ATPG framework tightly integrating structural algorithms with PA-MiniSat.
nv: First SAT solver supporting partial assignments for test pattern generation, reducing specified bits in test cubes.
th: SAT-based ATPG with partial assignment for improved test compaction

t: Late Breaking Results: Warpage-Aware Generative Floorplanning for Reliable Advanced Packaging
pb: Advanced IC packaging introduces heterogeneous materials and dense interconnects, causing thermal warpage that degrades system performance and reliability during floorplanning optimization.
me: A transformer-based encoder learns node and edge representations from the floorplan graph. Parallel decoding combined with warpage-aware legalization jointly minimizes die displacement and warpage distortion, integrating thermal-mechanical coupling constraints into the optimization loop.
nv: First warpage-aware generative floorplanning algorithm using transformer-based encoding and joint optimization of die displacement and warpage effects.

mx.other: 9.9% warpage improvement, 8.3% wirelength reduction

th: Warpage-aware AI-guided floorplanning for advanced packaging reliability

t: Process-Variation-Aware Design Optimization for Wavelength-Routed Optical Networks-on-Chip
pb: Wavelength-routed optical NoCs use microring resonators (MRRs) for collision-free communication, but manufacturing process variation shifts MRR transmission spectra, reducing signal power and increasing crosstalk.
me: Methodology constructs analytical models of expected signal transmission power under MRR process variation. Optimization jointly tunes MRR radii and signal wavelengths to maximize expected signal power despite process variation. Joint tuning exploits coupled effects between geometry and wavelength selection.
nv: First process-variation-aware design optimization for wavelength-routed optical NoCs, analytically modeling MRR variation and jointly optimizing radii and wavelengths.

mx.other: 7.51 dB signal transmission power improvement

th: Variation-aware optical NoC design via joint MRR and wavelength optimization

t: DBC: Drift-aware Binary Code for Drift-tolerant Deep Neural Networks
pb: Phase change memory (PCM) cells with multi-level (MLC) operation suffer from conductance drift over time, causing significant accuracy degradation in DNNs stored in PCM.
me: Proposes Drift-aware Binary Code (DBC), a novel binary encoding that maps smaller decimal values to less error-prone PCM cell levels and ensures values shift toward smaller magnitudes upon drift. This maintains DNN accuracy over extended periods because dominant weights are stored at drift-resistant levels, and DNNs tolerate weight decreases better than increases. DBC requires no additional hardware overhead and combines with ECC.
nv: First binary code design specifically optimized for PCM conductance drift, mapping values to minimize drift-induced errors through magnitude-aware encoding.
th: Drift-aware binary encoding for PCM-based DNN storage

t: Machine Learning-Driven STL Generation for Enhancing Functional Safety of E/E Systems
pb: Traditional functional safety testing methods like ATPG and BIST are intrusive, requiring additional hardware and disrupting normal operations, making them unsuitable for in-field testing in safety-critical systems.
me: Proposes ML-driven automated Self-Test Library (STL) generation using reinforcement learning to create design-specific test patterns for seamless in-field testing during idle periods. The RL agent learns to generate effective test patterns that avoid operation disruption while maintaining high fault coverage.
nv: First reinforcement learning-driven STL generation enabling design-specific, non-intrusive in-field testing for functional safety.
th: ML-driven STL generation for in-field functional safety testing

t: FastPath: A Hybrid Approach for Efficient Hardware Security Verification
pb: Microarchitectural information leakage verification methods suffer individual weaknesses: formal methods lack scalability, simulation lacks exhaustiveness, and existing approaches have limited flexibility for changing security requirements.
me: FastPath combines simulation efficiency with formal verification exhaustiveness via a hybrid methodology that employs structural analysis to automate the verification process, enabling practical deployment in existing verification flows.
nv: Hybrid simulation-plus-formal verification framework with structural automation for microarchitectural security verification.

mx.other: Significant reduction in manual verification effort with same exhaustiveness level

th: Hybrid formal-simulation security verification with structural automation

t: MemSeer: Leverage Memory Failure Distinctions and Multi-Grained Prediction in Ultra-Scale Heterogeneous X86/ARM Clusters
pb: In ultra-scale heterogeneous cloud clusters mixing x86 and ARM platforms, DRAM failures are a primary cause of server downtime; existing prediction methods fail to account for architecture-specific failure patterns and require single-scale predictions.
me: MemSeer analyzes memory failure characteristics across x86/ARM platforms and employs multi-grained prediction (multiple timescale levels) integrated into AIOps to predict failures. Achieves 17.3% F1-score improvement and 27% recall improvement.
nv: Architecture-aware multi-grained memory failure prediction exploiting x86/ARM failure distinctions for heterogeneous cluster reliability.

mx.other: 17.3% F1-score improvement, 27% recall improvement, 42.7% VM interruption reduction

th: Architecture-aware multi-grained DRAM failure prediction

t: Uncertainty-Aware Energy Management for Wearable IoT Devices with Conformal Prediction
pb: Energy management for battery-powered wearable IoT devices with stochastic ambient energy harvesting; existing point-prediction energy management methods do not account for prediction uncertainty.
me: Conformal prediction framework for future energy harvest that provides prediction intervals with provable coverage guarantees. Uncertainty regions are leveraged in a Monte Carlo sampling-based energy management algorithm that evaluates multiple decisions across sampled energy scenarios; results are aggregated via lightweight ML model to make near-optimal energy decisions.
nv: Conformal prediction-based approach for energy harvesting with quantified uncertainty, enabling probabilistic energy management decisions with coverage guarantees.

mx.accuracy: >90% coverage with tight prediction intervals; average 2 J from optimal Oracle
mx.other: Quality of service improvement in wearable IoT

th: Uncertainty-aware energy management for wearable IoT via conformal prediction

t: MEEK: Re-thinking Heterogeneous Parallel Error Detection Architecture for Real-World OoO Superscalar Processors
pb: Heterogeneous parallel error detection requires gathering data cross-chip from many core components to re-execute software, but integrating this into commodity out-of-order superscalar cores creates design complexity and risks heavy modifications to mature microarchitectures.
me: MEEK implements heterogeneous parallel error detection via co-designed hardware-software layers: a high-performance OoO core executes speculatively while power-efficient auxiliary cores re-execute the same code; coordinating software and light OS-level modifications orchestrate comparison and error reporting with microsecond-level latency. The design avoids invasive changes by partitioning responsibilities across ISA, microarchitecture, and operating system.
nv: First full-RTL implementation of heterogeneous parallel error detection in an open-source SoC that achieves microsecond-scale fault detection with minimal architectural disruption via codesigned hardware-software partitioning.

mx.other: microsecond-level detection latency, light design overhead

th: fault-tolerant processor design via parallel error detection

t: GraphFI: An Efficient Fault Injection Framework for Graph Processing on GPGPUs
pb: Existing fault injection methods ignore graph-specific execution paradigms (iterations, vertices, error propagation), producing inaccurate system error resilience characterization and blind fault injection trials that are computationally expensive.
me: GraphFI exploits three graph-specific properties: iteration-driven FI (selecting representative iterations with similar active vertex sets), topology-driven FI (identifying resilience-similarity communities and testing representative vertices), and monotonicity-driven FI (using fault monotonic properties to predict severe error boundaries). Merging all three approaches reduces fault site space by up to 100x.
nv: First graph-specific fault injection framework leveraging iteration, topology, and monotonicity properties to dramatically reduce FI trials (2.1-15.2x speedup) while improving reliability assessment accuracy.

mx.other: up to 100x reduction in fault site space

th: graph-specific fault injection for GPU reliability

t: Real-Time Dynamic IR-drop Prediction for IR ECO
pb: During IR Engineering Change Order (ECO) stages in chip design, cell moving causes unpredictable IR-drop changes, requiring designers to run expensive simulations for each ECO candidate to evaluate voltage integrity, making design iterations slow.
me: An XGBoost machine learning model with a global view of cell surroundings predicts dynamic IR-drop immediately after ECO without running any SPICE simulations. The model is trained to capture IR-drop variations for moved cells. After ECO, it provides predictions in minutes versus over an hour of simulation time, enabling concurrent evaluation of multiple ECO candidates in a single iteration.
nv: Real-time XGBoost-based IR-drop prediction post-ECO without simulation, replacing expensive SPICE runs and enabling parallelized ECO candidate evaluation.
th: ML-based real-time IR-drop prediction for ECO acceleration

t: FT-MUX: A Fault-Tolerant Microfluidic Multiplexer Design
pb: Microfluidic multiplexers enable routing through many flow channels with few control channels, but as integration scales up, control-channel defects affect large numbers of flow channels, creating reliability concerns.
me: FT-MUX formally analyzes design rules for multiplexers tolerating n defective control channels. Models fault-tolerant MUX design as binary constant weight code (BWCC) problem to minimize resource overhead while maintaining functionality. Determines conditions under which FT-MUX can address more flow channels than standard MUX with equal or fewer control channels.
nv: First formal framework for fault-tolerant microfluidic multiplexer design using coding theory optimization.

mx.other: resource efficiency improvement up to 100x

th: Fault-tolerant microfluidic multiplexer design via coding theory

t: H3Match: A Hybrid Heterogeneous Hypergraph Matching Method for Subcircuit Identification
pb: Subcircuit matching in circuit synthesis and verification is slow and inaccurate using prior GNN-based filtering that produces high false negatives and redundant circuit representations.
me: Models circuits as heterogeneous hypergraphs to capture topology, uses directed GNN-based approximate matching with DAG reformulation to reduce false negatives, and accelerates exact verification via MINLP formulation with warm-start solutions extracted from approximate matching.
nv: Hypergraph-based circuit representation with directed GNN matching that reformulates the problem as DAG matching with embedded circular structures to minimize false negatives.
th: Hypergraph GNN for subcircuit matching with low false negatives

t: RE3: Finding Refinement Relations with Relational Mapping Abstraction
pb: Manually constructing refinement relations between sequential circuits is tedious and error-prone, requiring deep domain knowledge and formal methods expertise, especially for post-transformation designs.
me: Develops rigorous sequential equivalence checking algorithm that automatically discovers concise, human-comprehensible refinement relations between two non-cycle-accurate designs using relational mapping abstraction.
nv: Automated refinement relation discovery via sequential equivalence checking with relational mapping abstraction, providing human-readable relation extraction.
th: Automated refinement relation discovery for sequential equivalence checking

t: AutoRE: Bayesian-Optimization-based Automatic Reliability Enhancement Tool for Flow-based Microfluidic Biochips
pb: Flow-based microfluidic biochips suffer from low yield due to manufacturing defects causing malfunctions; while reliability quantification models exist, automatic layout optimization to enhance reliability is lacking.
me: AutoRE uses Bayesian optimization to explore layout variants within predefined topology constraints, identifying the most reliable configuration. The system varies spatial dimensions and positions without changing connectivity.
nv: First automated tool to enhance microfluidic biochip reliability via Bayesian-optimized layout variant exploration.

mx.other: 40% average reliability improvement

th: Bayesian-optimized reliability enhancement for microfluidic biochips

t: Asymmetric Predictive Testing for Aging in SRAMs
pb: Current predictive testing methods for aging-induced SRAM failures use symmetric aggressive voltage conditions across read and write operations, resulting in significant over-testing that spuriously marks functional chips as defective.
me: The work identifies asymmetric aging in SRAM cells that preferentially store zeros and are more prone to read-1 failures. Proposes asymmetric testing: normal-voltage writes, aggressive-voltage read-0, and less-aggressive-voltage read-1. Introduces a statistical sampling and simulation method for fast convergence.
nv: Asymmetric predictive testing exploits cell-level asymmetric aging to reduce over-testing by 3-5× while maintaining under-testing limits.

mx.other: 3-5× over-testing reduction

th: asymmetric aging-aware predictive testing for SRAM

t: Simulation-based Parallel Sweeping: A New Perspective on Combinational Equivalence Checking
pb: Combinational equivalence checking (CEC) is co-NP-complete; SAT-based approaches dominate but timeout on large designs. GPU acceleration for simulation-based checking unexplored.
me: Exhaustive simulation-based CEC engine using GPU parallelism: distributes simulation across GPU cores to rapidly explore test patterns, achieving 88x speedup vs CPU SAT solver on specific large cases; hybrid with ABC when simulation alone insufficient.
nv: Simulation-based CEC perspective using GPU parallelism instead of SAT-based methods.
th: GPU-parallel simulation for combinational equivalence checking

t: Multicore Environment State Representation for Agent-Directed Test Generation
pb: Verification of multicore systems requires testing core interactions, but current test generation lacks an effective method to extract actionable state information from raw environment observations for learning-based optimization.
me: A reinforcement learning approach where an RL agent generates test programs executed in a multicore simulation environment (16 and 32-core ARMv8 with MOESI coherence). The agent learns from interaction how to improve verification coverage by recovering structured state information from raw environment observations.
nv: Effective state representation extraction from raw multicore observations to enable RL agents to learn directed test generation strategies for coherence and multi-core interaction verification.

mx.other: Verification coverage improvement (specific metrics not provided)

th: RL-driven test generation for multicore system verification

t: PoP-ECC: Robust and Flexible Error Correction against Multi-Bit Upsets in DNN Accelerators
pb: Continuous process scaling increases memory error severity and frequency in DNN accelerators, particularly multi-bit upsets (MBUs). Traditional single-error correction codes are insufficient for safety-critical systems.
me: Parities of Parities ECC (PoP-ECC) is a two-tier memory protection scheme. First level computes Virtual Parities (VPs) from data; second level computes Parities of Parities (PPs) from VPs. This hierarchical structure enables dynamic error correction tailored to varying error patterns with minimal overhead.
nv: Two-tier hierarchical ECC structure (Virtual Parities → Parities of Parities) enabling flexible MBU correction with tunable protection levels.

mx.other: tolerates higher MBU ratios; negligible delay, area, power overhead

th: hierarchical ECC for multi-bit upset protection

t: Late Breaking Results: Fine-Tuning LLMs for Test Stimuli Generation
pb: LLMs fine-tuned for hardware test stimuli generation often produce inconsistent or incorrect outputs; existing prompt engineering and feedback mechanisms do not effectively improve domain-specific performance in test generation.
me: Two-stage fine-tuning framework: first generates a table-shaped test stimuli dataset to ensure LLM output consistency, then applies reinforcement learning (RL) to provide corrective feedback on generated outputs. The approach trains LLMs on domain-specific data with RL signals tuned for test coverage and correctness.
nv: Domain-specific LLM fine-tuning via table-shaped dataset generation followed by RL feedback, specifically targeting test stimuli generation performance.

mx.other: improved syntax correctness and code coverage vs. commercial models

th: domain-specific LLM fine-tuning for test stimulus generation

t: X-SAT: An Efficient Circuit-Based SAT Solver
pb: Verifying equivalence of arithmetic circuits requires efficient SAT solving, but existing SAT solvers optimized for CNF struggle with circuit-specific structure and the high variable/clause counts in complex arithmetic circuits.
me: X-SAT integrates Conflict-Driven Clause Learning (CDCL) with structural elimination techniques that reduce variables and clauses while preserving circuit topology. It enhances branching heuristics specifically for arithmetic circuit structure to guide search more efficiently.
nv: Circuit-specific branching heuristics and structural elimination integrated into CDCL to exploit arithmetic circuit patterns that CNF-based approaches miss.

mx.other: faster than CNF-based SAT solvers on arithmetic circuits

t: No Rush in Executing Atomic Instructions
pb: Modern x86 processors implement unfenced atomic RMW instructions (no implicit serializing fences), enabling eager execution as soon as operands are ready, but eager execution locks cachelines early which prolongs the lock duration and harms other threads attempting to acquire the same contended cacheline. Conversely, lazy execution (waiting until the atomic is oldest in the load queue and the store buffer is empty) minimizes cacheline lock time but exposes full memory access latency on non-contended accesses.
me: Rush or Wait (RoW) is a hardware mechanism that dynamically selects between eager and lazy atomic execution via a 64-entry, 4-bit saturating-counter contention predictor indexed by the XOR of the 12 least-significant PC bits. At issue, the predictor determines the execution mode; at completion, it updates using three progressively refined contention detection mechanisms: (1) Execution Window (EW) — marks an atomic contended if an external coherence invalidation/downgrade arrives while the cacheline is locked; (2) Ready Window (RW) — extends tracking to the window from when the atomic's operands are ready by computing the address eagerly and snooping the Atomic Queue (AQ) for address matches on external requests; (3) Directory detection (RW+Dir) — additionally marks an atomic contended when the cacheline arrives from another core's private cache with latency exceeding a 400-cycle threshold, catching cases where contention is resolved before an external request reaches the core. Store-to-load forwarding from older regular stores overrides a lazy prediction to improve atomic locality. Total storage: 64 bytes (256-bit predictor + 256-bit AQ augmentation).
nv: The first analysis of the eager-vs-lazy execution trade-off for unfenced atomic RMWs, and a hardware contention predictor (RoW) that dynamically switches between eager and lazy atomic execution based on predicted cacheline contention with only 64 bytes of state.

pb: LLM-based hardware generation produces functional errors and structural flaws. Current approaches focus on direct generation, yielding 27-44% pass rates. Lack reasoning capability for complex structural constraints.
me: Multi-stage reasoning-enhanced training framework: (1) compilation filtering dataset curation achieving 100% pass rate, (2) function-aligned differentiated revision for comparative annotation across five RTL-relevant dimensions, (3) supervised fine-tuning using reasoning prompts, (4) reinforcement learning guided by Verilator parser for functional validation.
nv: Function-aligned differentiated revision methodology annotating RTL code across five dimensions, combined with reasoning-enhanced training.

mx.accuracy: 20% improvement in pass@1 on VerilogEval Human benchmarks

th: reasoning-enhanced LLM for hardware design

t: Revisiting Noise-adaptive Transpilation in Quantum Computing: How Much Impact Does it Have?
pb: Frequent noise-adaptive transpilation using up-to-date calibration data is widely considered essential but its necessity and overhead have not been thoroughly questioned.
me: Empirical study across five IBM 127-qubit quantum computers and 16 quantum algorithms investigating noise-aware transpilation necessity and effectiveness.
nv: Questions conventional wisdom about noise-adaptive transpilation necessity by showing random mapping can maintain comparable fidelity.

mx.other: error variability: reduced with random mapping

th: Rethinking necessity of frequent noise-adaptive transpilation

t: Row-Column Hybrid Grouping for Fault-Resilient Multi-Bit Weight Representation on IMC Arrays
pb: Analog IMC systems suffer from stuck-at faults (SAFs) that reduce computational reliability and existing fault-mitigation algorithms (e.g., Fault-Free) impose high compilation overhead. Fault-resilient design of IMC arrays remains computationally expensive and challenging to scale.
me: The paper proposes row-column hybrid grouping that generalizes column grouping by introducing redundancy across both rows and columns in weight representation. A compiler pipeline reformulates fault-aware weight decomposition as an Integer Linear Programming (ILP) task solved by off-the-shelf solvers. Theoretical insights identify fault patterns with trivial solutions, significantly reducing computation time while maintaining fault tolerance.
nv: 2D redundancy structure (row-column hybrid grouping) combined with ILP-based compilation for fast, scalable fault-aware weight decomposition in IMC arrays.

mx.other: fault tolerance and reliability enhancement

th: Fault-resilient IMC with 2D redundancy

t: Scalable and Asynchronous Differential Checkpointing for Intermittently Powered Devices
pb: Intermittently powered devices relying on checkpoint-recovery face scalability challenges: hardware-based differential checkpointing costs increase proportionally with memory size, and synchronous checkpointing blocks the MCU during backups, causing unacceptable latency.
me: FLASC is a hardware-software co-design enabling scalable and asynchronous differential checkpointing. The approach: (1) uses memory modification tracking that scales with increasing memory size; (2) supports safe asynchronous checkpoint execution allowing MCU to continue work during backups; (3) combines efficient synchronization mechanisms with reduced hardware overhead through smart software-hardware partitioning.
nv: Hardware-software co-designed differential checkpointing achieving scalability and asynchronous operation without proportional hardware cost growth.

mx.other: 6.9× better scalability with memory size; 1.85× efficiency per hardware resource

th: Scalable asynchronous checkpointing for intermittent devices

t: STAR: Improving Lifetime and Performance of High-Capacity Modern SSDs Using State-Aware Randomizer
pb: Lateral charge spreading (LCS) in high-capacity 3D NAND flash causes retention errors that significantly reduce SSD lifetime, particularly as stack heights increase.
me: STAR: state-aware data randomizer that proactively eliminates weak data patterns vulnerable to LCS. Uses dual-polarity read for error detection and adaptive error-aware read with analytical Vth drift estimation for correction.
nv: First data randomizer specifically targeting LCS-induced weak patterns in high-capacity 3D NAND SSDs.

mx.other: 2.3x lifetime improvement, 50% latency reduction

th: State-aware randomization to mitigate lateral charge spreading in 3D NAND

t: Self-Error Detection and Correction Techniques for Reliable and Efficient Selector-Only Memory
pb: Selector-Only Memory (SOM) devices face threshold voltage (Vth) drift and device variation, reducing read window margin and increasing error rate, particularly challenging for advanced manufacturing processes.
me: Securer: self-detection via dual-polarity read operation leveraging SOM's unique features; self-correction using analytical Vth drift estimation model to track drifted threshold voltage with adaptive error-aware read operations.
nv: First self-detection and self-correction technique for SOM without relying on external error correction codes.

mx.other: Negligible timing overhead

th: Self-error detection and correction for Selector-Only Memory

t: Software-Style Hardware Debugging: A Hardware Generation, Simulation and Debugging Framework
pb: Hardware verification still relies on traditional RTL workflows, creating a bottleneck in design-verification iteration efficiency and limiting the use of modern debugging techniques.
me: ComoPy framework enables host language native simulation with fine-grained tracing and breakpoints on HDL source lines, software-style hot-reloading for incremental debug-fix cycles, and dynamic switching between fast low-level RTL simulation and high-level HDL execution.

t: A Precision-Steerable Electromigration Solver with Physics-Informed Adaptive Graph Partitioning
pb: Solving Korhonen's equation for multi-segment interconnect line models becomes increasingly challenging as technology scales; traditional FEM-based methods are computationally expensive.
me: Physics-Informed Message Passing Neural network (PIMNEM) architecture for solving coupled multi-domain Korhonen equations; AdaptEM incorporates hierarchical graph partitioning with unsupervised training on subgraphs and fine-tuning with boundary constraints.

t: Wit-HW: Bug Localization in Hardware Design Code via Witness Test Case Generation
pb: Hardware bug localization remains difficult for large designs and deep bugs because existing techniques rely on single bug-triggering test cases, missing complex interactions in intricate systems.
me: Wit-HW transforms bug localization into a test generation problem, creating witness test cases (passing cases) beyond the initial failing case. Spectrum-based analysis compares execution differences between passing and failing cases to eliminate innocent statements. A mutation-based strategy generates effective witness test cases optimized for bug localization.
nv: Using witness test case generation (passing cases) combined with spectrum-based analysis to localize bugs in large hardware designs.

mx.other: 49% Top-1, 73% Top-5, 88% Top-10 bug localization

t: SERA-Float: A Soft Error Resilient Approximate Floating-Point Computing Format
pb: Approximate floating-point computing lacks resilience to soft errors, and interaction between approximation-induced errors and soft errors can cause exceptions or unexpected failures in DNN inference.
me: SERA-Float protects sign and exponent bits using error-correcting codes and maintains 8 valid mantissa bits instead of truncation. Critical bit tracking prevents overflow, underflow, and NaN exceptions. Narrower arithmetic units leverage the format for energy savings.
nv: Approximate floating-point format combining error-correcting codes for sign/exponent protection with critical bit tracking to prevent exceptions.
th: Soft error resilient approximation

t: PCBFormer: Understanding 3D Structure of RealWorld PCB Traces for S-Parameter Prediction
pb: S-parameter extraction for PCB traces via electromagnetic simulation is computationally expensive and becomes a bottleneck with iterative design changes in component placement.
me: PCBFormer is a deep learning framework capturing electromagnetic interactions across multiple layers in 3D PCB structures. The model accounts for each layer's properties and multiple traces' coupling effects to predict S-parameters across frequency ranges from DC to 1 GHz.
nv: Deep learning framework capturing multi-layer 3D PCB trace interactions for rapid S-parameter prediction.

mx.other: 0.86 R² for S-parameter prediction (DC-1GHz)

th: PCB simulation via deep learning

t: GeoFA - 2D layout pattern matching using deterministic finite automaton
pb: Layout pattern matching in chip design is computationally expensive, requiring search through millions of geometric patterns to verify design rules or identify specific structures. Commercial tools like Calibre are slow for complex pattern searches.
me: GeoFA uses deterministic finite automaton to encode 2D layout patterns and perform efficient matching against chip layouts, converting geometric pattern specifications into DFA states and transitions.
nv: Application of DFA-based automaton theory to 2D layout pattern matching, achieving dramatic speedup over conventional geometric search.
th: Automaton-based layout pattern matching

t: PROFUZZ: Directed Graybox Fuzzing via Module Selection and ATPG-Guided Seed Generation
pb: Directed hardware fuzzing struggles with precise seed generation for specific submodules, suffering from limited HDL support, abstraction mismatches, and poor scalability for large designs.
me: PROFUZZ integrates Automatic Test Pattern Generation (ATPG) with directed graybox fuzzing (DGF), leveraging ATPG's structural analysis for seed generation. Supports module-level targeting with improved scalability through ATPG-based constraint generation.
nv: ATPG-guided seed generation for directed hardware fuzzing enabling precise module-level testing.
th: ATPG-guided directed fuzzing for hardware verification

t: Target Circuit Matching in Large-Scale Netlists Using GNN-Based Region Prediction
pb: Subgraph matching in circuit verification struggles with large-scale circuits; traditional rule-based methods lack generalization, and node-to-node approaches are computationally inefficient.
me: Proposes GNN-based approach predicting regions of high probability for containing target circuits. Constructs negative samples for accurate target circuit detection, develops method to directly extract subgraph embeddings capturing global information, avoiding inefficient per-candidate GNN application.
nv: GNN-based region prediction for efficient subgraph matching reducing per-candidate computation.

mx.method: time efficiency and region prediction accuracy

th: GNN-based efficient subgraph matching for circuit verification

t: BMCFuzz: Hybrid Verification of Processors by Synergistic Integration of Bound Model Checking and Fuzzing
pb: RISC-V processor verification requires exhaustive checking of instruction semantics and corner cases, which is computationally expensive using pure formal methods or fuzzing alone.
me: Integrate bounded model checking with fuzzing: use BMC to verify instruction behavior formally within bounded execution depth, guide fuzzing with BMC-discovered constraints to find edge cases beyond formal bounds. Synergistic feedback loop between both techniques for RISC-V ISA compliance.
nv: Synergistic integration of BMC and fuzzing for efficient RISC-V processor verification with improved corner-case detection.
th: hybrid BMC-fuzzing for RISC-V processor verification

t: ISO 26262-Aligned Functional Safety Verification Framework with Explainable Graph Neural Network
pb: Automotive functional safety verification (ISO 26262) requires exhaustive fault injection analysis; traditional simulation-based approaches are slow and lack interpretability for safety certification.
me: Develop GNN model trained on circuit fault injection data to predict functional safety criticality. Use explainable GNN (e.g., graph attention) to identify fault propagation paths and safe design points. Validate against standard fault injection benchmarks.
nv: Explainable GNN framework for ISO 26262 functional safety verification with interpretable fault propagation analysis.
th: explainable GNN for ISO 26262 automotive functional safety verification

t: COTIA: Concolic Testing with Intelligent Agent
pb: Concolic testing for hardware verification suffers from suboptimal path exploration due to local optima in heuristics, leading to incomplete coverage of corner cases.
me: Agent-based framework using beam search and large language models to dynamically adjust path exploration strategies in concolic testing simulation.
nv: First to apply LLM-guided agents with beam search for optimizing path exploration in hardware concolic testing.
th: AI-guided hardware verification and testing

t: RIROS: A Parallel RTL Fault SImulation FRamework with TwO-Dimensional Parallelism and Unified Schedule
pb: RTL fault simulation for safety-critical applications is time-consuming due to imbalanced task loads from dynamic fault propagation paths, slowing verification cycles.
me: Two-dimensional parallel framework combining structural-level and fault-level parallelism with work-stealing and unified computation/synchronization scheduling to minimize execution bubbles.
nv: First two-dimensional parallelism approach for RTL fault simulation balancing heterogeneous task loads.
th: Parallel RTL fault simulation for safety-critical chips

t: VeriSAT: the Hardware Design of Modern SAT Solver
pb: Traditional SAT solvers execute in software; hardware-accelerated approaches lack optimization for concurrent operations and efficient data structures.
me: First modern SAT solver in synthesizable SystemVerilog with hardware-optimized data structures: linked-list literal-watching, concurrent propagation tree, and pipelined clause learning.
nv: First fully-synthesizable SystemVerilog SAT solver with custom hardware-optimized data structures and parallelized processes.
th: Hardware-accelerated SAT solving with optimized datastructures

t: GROOT: Graph Edge Re-growth and Partitioning for the Verification of Large Designs in Logic Synthesis
pb: GNN-based verification for large circuits lacks joint framework considering chip domain knowledge, graph theory, and GPU optimization, leading to memory bottlenecks.
me: Algorithm-system co-design with polarized node feature extraction, graph partitioning algorithm with edge re-growth, and specialized GPU kernels (HD-kernel, LD-kernel) for high/low-degree node handling.
nv: First algorithm-system co-design framework for GNN-based logic synthesis verification with domain-specific GPU optimization.
th: GNN-based verification with GPU-optimized kernels for large circuits

t: SCArmor: Layer-Bit Joint Hardening with a Fast Genetic Optimization for Cost-Efficient and High-Reliable SC-DCNN Circuits
pb: Stochastic Computing-based Deep CNNs face radiation-induced errors affecting reliability in harsh environments.
me: Genetic algorithm for joint layer and bit-width selection. Optimizes hardening strategy for stochastic computing neural networks. Targets area, power, and latency reduction simultaneously.
nv: First genetic algorithm-based approach for layer-bit joint hardening in SC-DCNN circuits.
th: Radiation-hardened stochastic computing DNNs

t: Promise: Property Mining for Sequential Synthesis
pb: Sequential synthesis for removing redundant circuit logic depends critically on accurate invariant generation, but existing techniques are problem-specific or rely on localized reasoning, limiting their applicability to diverse circuit designs with modular composition.
me: Proposes Promise, a fast circuit redundancy removal strategy that exploits rich information from simulation traces to infer global circuit invariants using efficient polynomial-time algorithms. Identifies relations between signals and registers that hold in all reachable states. Integrates with high-level synthesis tools to optimize generated circuits and aid other sequential synthesis procedures.
nv: First trace-based global invariant inference approach for sequential synthesis using polynomial-time algorithms, enabling practical redundancy removal in HLS-generated circuits.
th: Trace-based invariant mining for circuit synthesis

t: From Concept to Practice: an Automated LLM-aided UVM Machine for RTL Verification
pb: UVM testbench development is time-consuming and requires deep hardware verification expertise. Manual testbench creation is error-prone and labor-intensive.
me: LLM-based framework (UVM2) that generates UVM testbenches from RTL specifications with coverage feedback loop. Uses LLM to synthesize test sequences and constraints. Achieves 38.82× reduction in testbench setup time and 87.44% code coverage.
nv: LLM-driven automated UVM testbench generation with integrated coverage feedback for improved test quality.
th: LLM-aided UVM testbench generation

t: Equivalent Lumped Element Model for Electromigration Considering Thermal Effects
pb: Traditional physics-based electromigration (EM) analysis using partial differential equations (PDEs) is computationally intensive, particularly in multi-physics scenarios with thermal coupling.
me: Self-consistent lumped element modeling framework leveraging equivalence between electrical behavior and stress evolution; embedded controlled sources model thermomechanical interactions driven by temperature gradients; threshold-activated switching dynamically reconfigures circuit topology for void nucleation and post-voiding phases; adaptive non-uniform spatial discretization enhances computational efficiency. Fully compatible with standard SPICE solvers.
nv: Lumped element equivalent circuit approach for EM modeling with explicit electro-thermomechanical coupling, enabling SPICE simulation.
th: EM reliability analysis

t: Unified Memory Protection with Multi-granular MAC and Integrity Tree for Heterogeneous Processors
pb: Hardware memory protection in heterogeneous SoCs (CPU + GPU + NPU) causes significant performance degradation because conventional fixed-granularity MACs and integrity trees are optimized for CPU access patterns but perform poorly under the diverse, irregular memory access patterns of GPUs and NPUs.
me: The authors propose a unified multi-granular MAC and integrity tree mechanism that supports four granularity levels for both MACs and counters. A multi-granular tree stores coarse-grained and fine-grained counters at different tree levels, and a dynamic detection mechanism selects the most appropriate granularity per memory region based on the observed access pattern from each processing unit. The design is further combined with prior sub-tree techniques to reduce tree traversal overhead.
nv: The unified multi-granular MAC and tree mechanism is the first device-independent approach supporting adaptive granularity selection for both MACs and integrity tree counters simultaneously, enabling efficient memory protection across heterogeneous CPU/GPU/NPU access patterns.

mx.speedup: 14.2% execution time reduction over fixed-granular MAC and tree; 21.1% with sub-tree techniques

th: Adaptive multi-granular memory integrity protection for heterogeneous SoC processors

t: Lumina: Real-Time Neural Rendering by Exploiting Computational Redundancy
pb: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) neural rendering is computationally demanding for mobile SoCs, with high rasterization costs and redundant computation across temporally-coherent frames preventing real-time performance.
me: Lumina integrates two algorithmic optimizations: S2 (Spatial-temporal Skipping) exploits temporal coherence to skip recomputation of unchanged Gaussian contributions across frames, and RC (Radiance Caching) caches intermediate color integration values to reduce rasterization frequency. The LuminCore hardware accelerator is co-designed with these algorithms to efficiently support cache lookups and address rasterization inefficiencies inherent in the standard 3DGS pipeline on mobile hardware.
nv: The combination of temporal-coherence-based Gaussian skipping (S2) and radiance caching (RC) reduces both compute and rasterization frequency, enabled by a purpose-built mobile accelerator (LuminCore).

mx.energy_or_tops_w: 5.3x energy reduction over mobile Volta GPU

th: Hardware-algorithm co-design for real-time 3DGS neural rendering on mobile SoCs

t: Variational Quantum Algorithms in the era of Early Fault Tolerance
pb: Emerging 10,000-qubit devices with ~0.1% two-qubit error rates enable lightweight quantum error correction (QEC) but cannot afford the full qubit overhead of surface codes near threshold, leaving a regime—Early Fault Tolerance (EFT)—where error correction is partial and resource allocation strategy is unclear. Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) must be adapted to exploit EFT resources efficiently without the hardware or qubit budget of full fault tolerance.
me: The work introduces partial QEC (pQEC) for VQAs in the EFT regime, which error-corrects Clifford operations using lightweight codes while performing non-Clifford (Rz) rotations via magic state injection rather than the more expensive T-state distillation. Architectural optimizations reduce circuit latency by 2x, and a qubit packing strategy achieves 66% qubit efficiency in the EFT regime. The approach is evaluated by comparing fidelity gains of pQEC-VQA against standard (uncorrected) VQA approaches across multiple EFT device parameter settings.
nv: Adapting partial quantum error correction—Clifford-corrected with magic-state-injected non-Clifford rotations—to Variational Quantum Algorithms in the Early Fault Tolerance regime, achieving 9.27x fidelity improvement without requiring full surface-code QEC overhead.

mx.other: 2x circuit latency reduction; 66% qubit packing efficiency

th: Partial quantum error correction for variational algorithms in early fault tolerance

t: Synchronization for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers
pb: Logical qubits encoded with the surface code in fault-tolerant quantum computers (FTQC) can become desynchronized across their syndrome generation cycles due to heterogeneous QEC codes (color, qLDPC), fabrication defects causing extended clock cycles, and modular chip-to-chip coupling latencies. Lattice Surgery merge operations require all involved patches to begin their next syndrome generation cycle in lockstep, so desynchronized patches must idle—accumulating decoherence errors—before the operation can proceed.
me: Three synchronization policies are defined for the surface code with Lattice Surgery: (1) Passive—leading patch idles for the full synchronization slack immediately before the merge; (2) Active—slack is distributed as small idle fragments inserted after every QEC round, so no single idle window accumulates large decoherence; (3) Hybrid—for patches with unequal cycle times, runs extra rounds of error correction to reduce the residual slack, then applies Active for the remainder. A hardware microarchitecture consisting of a Patch Counter Table, Phase Calculators, and a Synchronization Slack Calculator determines patch phases at runtime and injects barrier instructions into the QEC controller schedule without adding latency to the critical path.
nv: Active synchronization proactively distributes the total idling slack across multiple QEC rounds, reducing peak decoherence per round and cutting the logical error rate by up to 3.4x over baseline passive idling.

mx.speedup: 2.2x reduction in decoding latency (Hybrid vs. Passive)
mx.accuracy: 3.4x reduction in logical error rate (Hybrid vs. Passive); 2.4x reduction (Active vs. Passive)
mx.other: Validated on IBM Brisbane 127-qubit and IBM Sherbrooke quantum hardware

th: Logical qubit synchronization policies for fault-tolerant quantum computing

t: Neoscope: How Resilient Is My SoC to Workload Churn?
pb: Hardware lifetimes are increasing while software workloads evolve rapidly, so SoCs optimized for today's workloads may perform poorly against future workloads; architects lack quantitative tools to design for long-term performance resilience.
me: Neoscope introduces two workload-change metrics, Magnitude and Disruption, that quantitatively characterize how a workload evolves over time, classifying churn as Minimal, Perturbing, Escalating, or Volatile. Using these metrics, Neoscope formulates SoC design space exploration as an integer linear program (ILP) combined with job-shop scheduling concepts, enabling it to find near-globally-optimal SoC configurations for a given churn span in a single invocation rather than requiring exhaustive parameter sweeps. The framework is multi-objective and can optimize simultaneously for performance, area, energy, cost, and carbon efficiency.
nv: First multi-objective pre-silicon design space exploration framework that explicitly models workload churn using ILP-based optimization to find churn-resilient SoC configurations in one shot.

mx.other: Neoscope approaches globally optimal SoC with a single invocation; shows small SoCs require high specialization but are more vulnerable to churn

th: workload-churn-aware SoC design space exploration

t: Precise exceptions in relaxed architectures
pb: The classical definition of precise exceptions assumes a sequential programmer's model and is inadequate for modern architectures like Arm-A that expose relaxed memory behavior; no formal specification exists for what exception precision means in a relaxed-memory setting.
me: The authors develop an axiomatic model for Arm-A precise exceptions in the relaxed-memory setting. They identify key phenomena—including relaxed behavior across exception boundaries, external aborts, and software-generated interrupts—that any definition must account for. A toolchain for axiomatic model execution is built, accompanied by a library of litmus tests that concretely characterize allowed and forbidden behaviors. The model is expressed in the style of existing Arm-A axiomatic memory models, extending them to cover exception entry and exit.
nv: The first formal axiomatic definition of exception precision for a real relaxed-memory architecture (Arm-A), resolving a decades-old open problem in architecture specification.

mx.other: Formal model correctness validated via litmus tests

th: Formal specification of precise exceptions under relaxed memory

t: SWIPER: Minimizing Fault-Tolerant Quantum Program Latency via Speculative Window Decoding
pb: Parallel window decoding for fault-tolerant quantum error correction requires some decoding tasks to be delayed until preceding windows complete, creating head-of-line blocking that inflates program runtime, especially during T gate teleportation where decoding latency directly extends logical circuit depth.
me: SWIPER introduces a speculative window decoder inspired by classical branch prediction. A lightweight speculation step predicts data dependencies between adjacent decoding windows, allowing multiple layers of decoding tasks to begin simultaneously rather than waiting for dependency resolution. If speculation is wrong, the decoder rolls back and re-decodes; the state-of-the-art compilation pipeline ensures that speculation opportunities are maximized. Performance is evaluated using a detailed open-source cycle-accurate simulator.
nv: Applying speculative execution—predicting inter-window data dependencies before they are resolved—to quantum error correction window decoders, eliminating blocking at window boundaries.

mx.speedup: 40% average application runtime reduction vs. prior parallel window decoders

th: Speculative window decoding for fault-tolerant quantum circuits

t: CORD: Low-Latency, Bandwidth-Efficient and Scalable Release Consistency via Directory Ordering
pb: In multi-processing-unit systems (CPU-GPU, multi-GPU) using write-through cache coherence with release consistency, the source processor must serialize write ordering through itself to the LLC directory, generating unnecessary round-trip communication that increases latency, interconnect traffic, and energy for producer-consumer AI/ML workloads.
me: CORD is a cache coherence protocol that relocates write-through ordering responsibility from the source processor to the LLC directory. The directory accumulates write-through operations and enforces release consistency locally, eliminating source-to-directory round-trips. Novel metadata compression mechanisms minimize the storage overhead of tracking in-flight ordered writes at the directory, and the protocol is designed to scale across multiple directories without serialization bottlenecks. Evaluation is performed on gem5.
nv: Moving release consistency enforcement of write-through accesses from the source processor to the cache directory, eliminating unnecessary source-ordering communication.

mx.speedup: 24% average performance improvement over source ordering
mx.other: 13% average traffic reduction; 3% overhead vs. hand-optimized message-passing

th: directory-ordered release consistency for multi-PU systems

t: Resource Analysis of Low-Overhead Transversal Architectures for Reconfigurable Atom Arrays
pb: Fault-tolerant quantum computation on neutral atom arrays using standard lattice-surgery gate schemes requires O(d) syndrome extraction (SE) rounds per logical gate, where d is the code distance, leading to run times of years for large-scale algorithms such as 2048-bit RSA factoring. Existing resource estimates do not account for transversal gates that reduce SE overhead to O(1) rounds per gate, nor do they provide detailed architectural layouts and logical error models for such schemes.
me: The architecture decomposes target quantum algorithms (benchmarked on Shor's 2048-bit factoring) into modular functional units—magic state factories (8T-to-CCZ distillation with |T> cultivation), ripple-carry quantum adders (Cuccaro MAJ/UMA gadgets with CCZ teleportation), and quantum look-up tables (QROM via GHZ-state-assisted CNOT fan-out)—all implemented using surface-code transversal gates with O(1) SE rounds per logical operation and correlated decoding. Atom movement uses direct optical tweezer shuttling with pipelined ancilla measurement to keep moves local and bounded (≤√2·d·l per step). A heuristic logical error model calibrated against MLE decoder simulations characterizes the elevated per-gate noise from transversal CNOTs via a decoding factor α≈1/6. Space-time trade-offs (bridge qubits, time-optimal computation with reaction-time offsets) are used to parallelize circuit segments and minimize total qubit-seconds.
nv: First complete large-scale transversal architecture with detailed subroutine layouts, a calibrated logical error model, and full resource estimation showing 50x run-time reduction for 2048-bit RSA factoring using O(1) SE rounds per transversal gate via correlated decoding on neutral atom arrays.

mx.speedup: ~50x run-time reduction vs. lattice-surgery baselines (Ref. [8],[9]) for 2048-bit RSA factoring on neutral atoms
mx.other: 19M qubits, 5.6 days at 1ms QEC cycle time; code distance d=27; up to 192 parallel magic state factories

th: transversal-gate fault-tolerant quantum architecture for neutral atom arrays

t: 8.8 Fine-Grained Spatial and Temporal Thermal Profiling of a 16nm CMOS Buck Converter and SoC Load-Current Emulator Using Low-Voltage Micron-Scale Thermal Sensors
pb: Localized thermal hotspots in high-power-density SoCs and 3D systems with integrated voltage regulators create fine-grained temperature gradients (>10°C across 100μm scales), limiting performance and reliability of AI/ML accelerators and special-purpose compute units.
me: The work develops low-voltage micron-scale thermal sensors for fine-grained spatial and temporal thermal profiling. A 16nm CMOS buck converter and SoC load-current emulator demonstrate the sensor architecture's ability to capture localized thermal hotspot profiles across heterogeneous workloads.
nv: Micron-scale thermal sensors in low-voltage CMOS enable real-time, fine-grained (100μm scale) thermal profiling of high-power-density SoCs.
th: On-chip thermal sensing for power management

t: 37.1 IBM Telum II Processor Design-Technology Co-Optimizations for Power, Performance, Area, and Reliability
pb: Designing a high-performance 5nm processor at scale requires simultaneous optimization of power, performance, area, and reliability while managing massive concurrent EDA and design complexity across libraries, IP blocks, and gate-level entities.
me: IBM Telum II implements full-stack design-technology co-optimizations on modified 5nm Samsung bulk CMOS. Key innovations include: (1) new IBM-created standard cell and IP libraries optimized jointly with process node, (2) concurrent hierarchical design where arrays, regfiles, analog blocks, PHY, and custom logic design simultaneously rather than sequentially, (3) integrated modeling and abstraction layers to manage design data volume and complexity.
nv: Concurrent hierarchical design methodology enables simultaneous library, IP, and gate-level development to manage 43B-transistor 5nm processor design complexity.
th: Design-technology co-optimization for 5nm processors

t: 8.4 A 4GHz, 0.69%-Accuracy Voltage-Droop Detector with Multiple Remote Sensing and Under 2-Cycle Detection Latency in 2nm GAAFET
pb: Voltage droop detection in modern SoCs requires both PVT-tolerant direct sensing and remote-capable distributed detection; previous digital detectors (TDC-based) suffer from PVT sensitivity and low conversion gain; analog detectors have bulky blocks, limited integration, and routing/frequency constraints.
me: 2nm GAAFET droop detector with compact distributed remote droop detectors (RDD) sampling at up to 4GHz, synchronized by a PVT-tolerant main droop detection controller (DDC), achieving <2-cycle latency with 0.69% accuracy.
nv: Distributed remote droop detectors with centralized PVT-tolerant control enabling high-frequency sampling without routing constraints.
th: Fast distributed voltage droop detection for per-core power scaling

t: 24.4 A 10b 3GS/s Time-Domain ADC with Mutually Exclusive Metastability Correction and Wide Common-Mode Input
pb: Time-domain (TD) ADCs suffer from unpredictable metastable trajectories in comparators that cause non-Gaussian error behaviors incompatible with low-bit-error-rate applications; prior metastability detection approaches constrain error probability gains by limiting available decision time on the critical path.
me: The 10b 3GS/s ADC decouples metastability detection constraints by pipelining comparator decisions with additional latches, allowing extended gain and time for unresolved-decision (UD) detection while maintaining multistep conversion speed through mutually exclusive correction logic.
nv: Pipelined unresolved-decision detection with mutually exclusive metastability correction maintaining multistep ADC latency while improving error probability.
th: High-speed time-domain ADC with metastability correction

t: 30.1 A 28Gb/mm24XX-Layer 1Tb 3b/Cell WF-Bonding 3D-NAND Flash with 5.6Gb/s/Pin IOs
pb: 3D NAND Flash scaling to higher layer counts (hundreds of layers) for density improvement creates multiple challenges: removal of dummy holes increases unselected string capacitance and power consumption; higher wordline counts amplify pass-voltage disturbance degrading cell reliability; increased wordline capacitance degrades program and read timing; high-speed I/O demands severe signal-integrity constraints.
me: 3D-NAND stack with WF-bonding (wafer-level) and multi-layer wordline architecture addressing: (1) dummy-hole removal via optimized cell-array design with high-density memory cells; (2) pass-voltage disturbance mitigation through efficient wordline structuring; (3) high-speed I/O support at 5.6Gb/s/pin via signal-integrity-aware pin design managing eye-width and eye-height constraints. Integration achieves 28Gb/mm2 at 3bits/cell (TLC NAND).
nv: WF-bonding 3D-NAND with optimized multi-layer wordline architecture and signal-integrity-aware I/O enabling high density, reliability, and speed simultaneously.
th: high-density, high-speed 3D-NAND through WF-bonding and optimized wordline design

t: 8.1 Dynamic Guard-Band Features of the IBM zNext System
pb: Fixed voltage guard bands at each supported frequency must cover all variation sources (power-supply droops, temperature excursions, device aging), consuming significant power even when worst-case conditions do not occur.
me: Full system that simultaneously leverages robust droop mitigation (e.g., on-chip power delivery management) and robust error recovery (e.g., voltage-independent correction codes or timeout mechanisms) to reduce required voltage margins in real-time using on-chip sensors and firmware.
nv: Combined approach that integrates droop mitigation and error recovery to dynamically reduce guard bands throughout the system.

t: Converos: Practical Model Checking for Verifying Rust OS Kernel Concurrency
pb: Verifying concurrent code in OS kernels is extremely difficult; traditional testing cannot guarantee the absence of race conditions, deadlocks, and other concurrency bugs in Rust OS kernel implementations.
me: Converos uses formal model checking to exhaustively explore the state space of concurrent kernel code, employing abstraction and state-space reduction techniques to make verification practical for real OS kernel implementations without exhaustive exploration becoming intractable.

t: Accelerated Design Verification Coverage Closure Using Machine Learning
pb: Design verification of complex ICs is bottlenecked by constrained random verification generating stimulus that does not provide incremental coverage, wasting simulation time and delaying time-to-market.

t: PPA-Aware Power Grid Optimization Techniques for Congested High Frequency Datapath Designs
pb: High-frequency networking switch designs require robust power grid optimization to handle congested signal routing while meeting stringent power, performance, and area (PPA) constraints, particularly regarding voltage drop and electromigration reliability.

t: ABMF: Adaptive Bonsai Merkle Forests for Efficient Integrity Verification in Secure Persistent Memories
pb: Non-volatile memory security verification using Merkle trees requires expensive tree traversal for MAC and counter updates on every memory write, creating significant latency and performance overhead.

t: TOGGLE6.0: A 4.8Gbps Next Generation Area and Power Efficient Transceiver for Flash Memory Interface
